story.title: Kay Granger, Pioneering Texas Congresswoman, Passes Away at 83
story.summary: Kay Granger, the first Republican woman from Texas elected to the U.S. House, has died at the age of 83. Granger served in Congress from 1997 until 2025 and was notable for being the first female chair of the House Appropriations Committee. Her passing was announced by fellow lawmakers.

explore_lenses.label: Was she the first woman to chair Appropriations?
explore_lenses.title: A historic first, with an important distinction
explore_lenses.summary: Granger was a barrier-breaking leader on the House Appropriations Committee, but the broader claim that she was its first female chair needs qualification.

claims.text: The House historian identifies New York Democrat Nita Lowey as the first woman to chair the House Appropriations Committee.

Granger became chair for the 118th Congress in 2023 and described herself as the first Republican woman to lead the committee; the House historian likewise calls her the first woman from the Republican Party to lead it.

points: The House historian identifies New York Democrat Nita Lowey as the first woman to chair the House Appropriations Committee.

Granger became chair for the 118th Congress in 2023 and described herself as the first Republican woman to lead the committee; the House historian likewise calls her the first woman from the Republican Party to lead it.

explore_lenses.label: What did her Appropriations leadership mean?
explore_lenses.title: She helped shape federal funding priorities
explore_lenses.summary: As chair of the House panel responsible for appropriations, Granger held a central role in setting House Republicans’ approach to annual federal spending bills.

claims.text: In announcing her chairmanship, Granger said the committee was responsible for federal funding and argued that it should reduce spending where possible while prioritizing national security.
Granger cited her prior leadership of the Defense Appropriations Subcommittee and the presence of service members and defense contractors in her district as reasons she emphasized military funding.
Her official House biography records that she chaired the full Appropriations Committee during the 118th Congress, from 2023 through January 2025.

explore_lenses.title: No—she had already left Congress
explore_lenses.summary: Granger’s death does not trigger a special election because she retired before the current Congress began; Texas voters had already elected a successor for the seat.

claims.text: Granger served Texas’ 12th District from January 3, 1997, through January 3, 2025, and did not seek reelection in 2024.
Republican Craig Goldman was elected in November 2024 to succeed Granger in Texas’ 12th District.
Granger said when she announced her retirement that she was encouraged by a new generation of district leaders and intended to complete her term.

story_report.summary: Kay Granger, the first Republican woman from Texas elected to Congress, has died at 83. She represented Texas’ 12th District from 1997 until January 2025, after choosing not to seek reelection in 2024. Republican Craig Goldman was elected to succeed her, meaning her death follows the conclusion of a nearly 28-year House career rather than creating a vacancy in the district’s seat.

sections.heading: Kay Granger’s Appropriations Leadership
sections.body: Granger chaired the House Appropriations Committee during the 118th Congress, from 2023 through January 2025. House historical records identify her as the first Republican woman to lead the panel, not its first woman chair; New York Democrat Nita Lowey was the first woman to chair the committee. In announcing her chairmanship, Granger said the committee should seek spending reductions where possible while prioritizing national security.

sections.heading: Kay Granger’s Texas House Service
sections.body: Granger served Texas’ 12th District from January 3, 1997, through January 3, 2025. She said when announcing her retirement that she was encouraged by a new generation of leaders in the district and intended to finish her term. Her appropriations priorities included military funding, which she linked to her earlier leadership of the Defense Appropriations Subcommittee and to service members and defense contractors in her district.

unresolved.text: The supplied summary’s description of Granger as the first female chair of the House Appropriations Committee is broader than the House historical record supports; that record identifies her as the first Republican woman to lead the committee.

related_stories.title: Todd Blanche Terminates Trump's Anti-Weaponization Fund Ahead of Confirmation Hearing
related_stories.summary: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche has rescinded the $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund initiated by President Donald Trump. This decision comes as Blanche prepares for his confirmation hearing and follows threats from GOP senators to block his appointment if he did not take action regarding the fund, which was intended to support Trump's political allies.

related_stories.title: Senate Leaders Agree on Short-Term Spending Bill to Prevent Government Shutdown
related_stories.summary: Senate leaders have reached a funding agreement aimed at preventing a government shutdown during the upcoming midterm elections. The short-term spending bill is expected to be voted on before the Senate's August recess, allowing lawmakers to focus on their reelection campaigns. This deal comes amid tensions with the White House regarding science funding and other budgetary issues.

related_stories.title: Iran Denies Ongoing Talks with U.S. Amid Trump's Claims of Progress
related_stories.summary: Iran has stated that there are no current negotiations or plans for meetings with the United States, contradicting President Trump's assertion of progress in talks that he cited as a reason for canceling planned military strikes. Trump had indicated that discussions regarding the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program were set to occur on the same day he called off the attacks.

related_stories.title: Israel Expresses Concerns Over Hamas Disarmament Amid Ongoing Strikes in Gaza
related_stories.summary: Israel has raised serious concerns regarding a proposed disarmament deal with Hamas, asserting that Hamas remains focused on military rebuilding rather than genuine demilitarization. This statement follows a series of Israeli airstrikes in Gaza that reportedly killed at least 19 individuals, including children, as Israel claims to target military operatives. The strikes have cast doubt on the viability of the peace plan proposed by President Trump.
